metadata.task_name: OIDC Auth Flow and Session Token Handling

execution.coverage: 100% — all four target files read and all OIDC code paths traced

finding.preliminary_assessment: The OIDC state parameter (VULN-003 fix) is consumed (removeItem) at line 58 BEFORE the validation comparison at line 59. This creates an ordering issue: if validation fails, the state is already gone — this is actually acceptable behavior (state should be single-use). However, the more significant issue is that if sendCodeAndConnectSession() at line 72 fails after canActivate() returns true, the session is orphaned: state consumed, code exchanged but token never stored, user stranded on /webLogin with broken retry capability. The catchError handler at line 73-76 logs the error and returns of(false) but does not clean up any partial session state. This is a medium-severity issue because it affects reliability of OIDC flow but does not directly enable session hijacking. The primary OIDC open redirect bypass (VULN-003) is the higher-severity finding from this same task.

patterns_observed: State nonce consumed at line 58 before validation at line 59 — ordering issue
Single-use consumption is correct behavior — the issue is post-failure cleanup
catchError at line 73-76 does not explicitly clean up orphaned session state
Username stored in sessionStorage as JSON.stringify(value) — unnecessary persistence risk
setNotConnected() does not explicitly remove oidc_state — relies on constructor clear()

false_positives.pattern: State not stored — race condition on OIDC redirect
false_positives.rationale: State is stored synchronously at line 43 before the async subscribe callback; actual redirect at line 67 is inside subscribe — state is always stored before redirect

analysis.coverage_assessment: Complete — full OIDC flow analyzed. Multiple secondary findings noted; primary finding (state ordering) is medium severity.
